windows_budget_basis: Measured wall time in run 36077289779 (windows-latest, 4 vCPU, prefix-matched dependency cache) x1.5, rounded up to 5: root-lib 46.0 (35.2 compile + 8.1 tests), root-sessions 30.8 (24.0 + 4.3), root-journeys 54.4 (38.7 + 10.9), root-transport 57.7 (38.0 + 17.3 with 36 failures and one hung test), root-dashboard-api 40.6 (34.4 + 3.3), runtime 66.5 (48.4 + 14.8), core-storage 36.5 (27.5 + 6.3), core-contracts 44.5 (39.4 + 2.5). The wider headroom is for this runner class: the archive lane's one workspace build measured 64.8 and 106.5 min on the same cache key (docs/ci-release-timing-census.md).
macos_budget_basis: Each group's budget is measured wall time plus headroom. Partition costs on macos-14 (3 vCPU), runs 36051245663, 36077289779, 36087768140 and 36095356282: root-lib 21.7-24.8 compile + 4 tests; root-sessions 20.0-25.9 + 3-4; root-journeys 6.1-7.4 + 3.4 against the sessions tree; root-transport 18.2-20.2 + 12.4 (one hung test, ~3 without); root-dashboard-api 0.9 + 0.7 against the transport tree (24.4 + 0.8 as a lone `-p tracedecay` resolution); runtime 28.5-29.6 + 5-6; core-storage 13.0-18.6 + 2.7; core-contracts 20.0-25.1 + 12.3 (one hung test, 0.5 without). The dependency cache does not move these: with every dependency unit from source (604 units, no cache) and with a full-match cache (3 units) the runtime, core-storage and core-contracts compiles were within a minute of each other, because on three cores the serial workspace chain and the test targets are the whole path and the dependency units fill the slots beside it. Groups therefore pair partitions of one resolution (the root suites, the transport pair) and otherwise balance the sums.
